claims.explanation: Amisulpride is a dopamine D2/D3 receptor antagonist, and its selective antiproliferative effect across cancer lines is most plausibly explained by expression of its primary target DRD2 (and related dopamine receptor pathway activity) in a subset of tumors, where receptor blockade inhibits proliferation or survival signaling. The pattern of sensitive lines (gastric, pancreatic, lung, melanoma, Ewing sarcoma) is not explained by a single common driver mutation, but several sensitive lines carry PI3K pathway alterations (PIK3CA mutation/amplification, PTEN loss) that may cooperate with DRD2 signaling, while many resistant lines have intact or alternative survival pathways. Thus DRD2 expression is the strongest predicted sensitizing feature, with PI3K pathway activation as a possible secondary

features.basis: primary drug target; D2 antagonism requires receptor expression for activity
amisulpride binds D3 with high affinity (Ki 3.2 nM)
PI3K activation observed in multiple sensitive lines (HGC27, MKN1, T47D, KYSE70, SNU840)
PTEN loss in sensitive lines (DMS273, TE4) may enhance dependence on survival signaling
TP53 mutation is near-universal in sensitive lines but also common in resistant lines, so weak
KRAS mutation in several sensitive pancreatic/gastric lines (SW1990, QGP1, GSU, PK45H)
BRAF mutation in sensitive melanoma lines (HS939T, K029AX)
ARID1A mutation in several sensitive lines (EFE184, T47D, KYSE70, OVTOKO, MHHNB11)
CDKN2A loss in sensitive lines (LXF289, HS939T, K029AX, MHHES1)
CTNNB1 mutation in resistant lines (KE39, HEC265) and one sensitive line, weak
NF2 mutation in resistant lines (SNU840 sensitive but NCIH2052, LCLC103H resistant), weak
KMT2D mutation enriched in resistant lines (KE39, HEC265, SNUC5, MFE319, PC14)
